{{nihongo|'''Oshisaka Yamaguchi Numasu Shrine'''|忍坂山口坐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

{{wikidata link|Q48763696|ja|忍坂山口坐神社|grok=none|check_date=2026-06-06}}

[[File:Oshisakayamaguchinimasu Jinja Kusunoki.jpg|thumb|220px|Giant camphor tree (designated cultural property of Sakurai City)]]

'''Oshisaka Yamaguchi-ni-masu Shrine''' (おしさかやまぐちにますじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|Q127026|qid=Q127026}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内大社|simple|Shikinai Taisha|qid=Q134917288}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is one of the six Yamaguchi shrines within {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Norito|de|Norito|es|Norito|fa|نوریتو|fr|Norito|gl|Norito|id|Norito|it|Norito|ja|祝詞|pl|Norito|ru|Норито|te|నోరిటో|tr|Norito|uk|Норіто|zh|祝詞|qid=Q1760119}}—namely, {{ill|Asuka-ni-Imasu Shrine|ja|飛鳥坐神社|qid=Q11665959|lt=Asuka}}, Iwaki, Oshisaka, Hase, {{ill|Unebiyamaguchi Shrine|ja|畝火山口神社|qid=Q11578590|lt=Unebi}}, and {{ill|Miminashi Yamaguchi Shrine|ja|耳成山口神社|qid=Q11610732|lt=Miminashi}}—and is one of the eighty-five shrines of the rain-prayer deities.

=== Enshrined deity ===
'''{{ill|Ōyamatsumi|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto}}'''

Descriptions regarding the identity of the enshrined deity are as follows:

* *Yamato Meisho Zue*: “Currently called the deity Ten’ichi.”
* *Yamato-shi*: “Now called Ten’ichi no Kami.”
* *Shūshōgatsu Kanjō Shinmeichō*: “The Ten’ichi Daimyōjin of this place.”
* *Gōsonsha Torishirabechō*: “Enshrined deity: Ten’ichi Shinmei Daimyōjin.”
* *{{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}*: “Enshrined deity: the mountain god Ōyamatsumi-no-Mikoto (omitted)… currently called Ten’ichi.”
* *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}*: “Enshrined deity: Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami.”

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
The date of founding is unknown. A record concerning Oshisaka Shrine estates appears in the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} ({{ill|730|ab|730|af|730|am|730 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|730|ar|730|ary|730|ast|730|az|730|azb|۷۳۰ (میلادی)|ban|730|be|730|be_x_old|730|bg|730|bn|৭৩০|bpy|মারি ৭৩০|br|730|bs|730.|ca|730|cdo|730 nièng|ceb|730|ckb|٧٣٠|crh|730|cs|730|cv|730|cy|730|da|730|de|730|el|730|eml|730|eo|730|es|730|et|730|eu|730|fa|۷۳۰ (میلادی)|fi|730|fo|730|fr|730|fy|730|ga|730|gan|730年|gd|730|gl|730|he|730|hi|730|hr|730.|ht|730 (almanak jilyen)|hu|730|hy|730|id|730|io|730|is|730|it|730|ja|730年|jv|730|ka|730|kaa|730|kk|730 жыл|ko|730년|la|730|lb|730|lij|730|lmo|730|lt|730 m.|map_bms|730|mdf|730|mg|730|mhr|730|mk|730|mr|इ.स. ७३०|mrj|730 и|ms|730|mzn|۷۳۰|nah|730|nap|730|nds|730|new|सन् ७३०|nl|730|nn|730|no|730|nrm|730|nso|730|oc|730|or|୭୩୦|os|730-æм аз|pl|730|pnb|730|pt|730|qu|730|ro|730|ru|730 год|rue|730|sa|७३०|sah|730|scn|730|sd|730ع|sh|730.|shn|730|si|730|sk|730|sl|730|smn|730|sq|730|sr|730|su|730|sv|730|sw|730|tg|Соли 730|th|พ.ศ. 1273|tk|730|tl|730|tly|730|tr|730|tt|730 ел|uk|730|ur|730ء|uz|730|vec|730|vi|730|war|730|wuu|730年|xmf|730|zh|730年|zh_min_nan|730 nî|zh_yue|730年|qid=Q23563}}) in the *{{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495|lt=Great Yamato Province}} Shōzeichō*. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daidō}} ({{ill|807|Q30016|qid=Q30016}}), one household of {{ill|Shinpo|Q1689534|qid=Q1689534}} was donated (as recorded in the *{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}*). In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as a major shrine and recorded as receiving offerings at the monthly and Niiname festivals.

According to an on-site guide (Sakurai City Tourism Association), in the 4th year of {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} ({{ill|1397|Q6410|qid=Q6410}}), when {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kinkaku-ji}} was constructed, a giant camphor tree sacred to this shrine was felled and used for the ceiling boards. During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, the shrine was known as “Ten’ichi Daimyōjin.” In the 37th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1904|Q2046|qid=Q2046}}), under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}}, it was ranked as a village shrine.

=== Court rank ===
* On {{ill|January 27|Q2284|qid=Q2284}}, 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten’an}} ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), promoted from Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade to Senior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (*{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}*). The notation used is “Oshisaka Yamaguchi Shrine.”

=== Precincts ===
Immediately to the left upon entering the precincts stands a giant camphor tree with a circumference of 7.3 meters, a height of 25 meters, and a height of 2 meters from the base. It is estimated to be over 500 years old and is designated as a cultural property of Sakurai City.

=== Access ===
* Approximately 800 meters southeast from {{ill|Yamato-Asakura Station|Q8047967|qid=Q8047967}} on the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Osaka Line}} of {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085}}
